sources.entry: Diurna - Basic/Classic Hacker News app, used as a Cocoa & Swift learning platform.

summary.one_liner: Diurna is a basic, classic-style Hacker News client for macOS, built with AppKit and Swift as a Cocoa learning project.
summary.what_it_does: The repository contains a macOS AppKit application (the "App" project) and a separate framework (HackerNewsAPI) that handles all calls to the official Hacker News API. Setup requires creating your own Firebase project and placing its GoogleService-Info.plist in App/Resources, with the DATABASE_URL key pointing to the official HN API URL. Dependencies are managed with CocoaPods via pod install. The README's TODO list mentions planned but unfinished items such as user preferences, comment folding fixes, code block layout fixes, a comment row height cache, login and voting, polls, a proper toolbar, and search. The author states the code is rough and the git history is messy.
use_cases: Browsing Hacker News on a Mac
Studying a real AppKit and Swift codebase
Learning Cocoa app architecture with a framework split
Reference for calling the official Hacker News API from Swift
how_to_run: Place GoogleService-Info.plist in the App/Resources directory, with DATABASE_URL set to the official HN API URL
Run pod install in the project directory to fetch CocoaPods dependencies
Open the workspace in Xcode and build the App project
notable: Split into an AppKit app and a separate HackerNewsAPI framework for API access
Designed as a learning project for Cocoa and Swift
Uses the official Hacker News API through Firebase configuration
caveats: The author warns the code is messy, only worked on occasionally, and the git history is poor
Requires a personal Firebase project and GoogleService-Info.plist before it will run
Many features are listed as TODO, including login, voting, and preferences
